notes: No blocking finding reached this stage -- PRIOR_FINDINGS, CARRIED_FINDINGS and ADVISORY_FINDINGS were all empty -- so no finding_dispositions are reported. The stage ran again because study-review at iteration 2 sent the run back into author-study, which repaired the expansive study through iterations 3 to 7 before its cold review passed at iteration 7; every derived document is re-derived when the study is repaired. The study's evidence did not move: propers/verified.md, research/scope.md, research/interpretations.md, research/context.md, research/chronology.toml, research/chronology-annotations.tex and research/source-bindings.toml carry the same digests at study-review iteration 7 that they carried at iteration 2. Only the study's prose changed, and four of those changes reach the companion. (1) STU-009: the study's gloss on Chrysostom's 'Because this makes the way for that, and by it is again established' now gives both clauses to the second commandment and its closing comparison reads 'mutual dependence in both directions'; the companion had quoted the sentence without a gloss and summarized the mechanism as 'mutual establishment', and now carries the study's gloss and its summary. (2) STU-010 and STU-012: the study withdrew the assertion that the Postcommunion's sanctificationes name a holiness God's own and given in the sacrament, and its comparison now says outright that the prayer gives the second reading nothing of its own; the companion still listed it as the third of three orations that reading hears as confession, which the accepted study now contradicts, and it now names two and states the disclaimer with the study's three grounds. (3) STU-016: the study restored the masculine member of Augustine's sentence at the Alleluia and states the unus/unum contrast in English; the companion never carried the defective gloss, and now carries the distinction and what the second reading draws from it. (4) STU-014: the companion's first use of Ps 109 now reads Ps 109:1 (Heb. 110:1), as the profile and the study's own stated convention require. Three further study repairs were checked and not copied because they do not reach this document: the running-head geometry and short running forms of format.tex (VIS-001, VIS-002), which this document inherits and whose heads already satisfy it; the longhand citation of the general rubrics (STU-015), in a passage the companion does not reproduce; and the References note on the NPNF1 10 editor's 'Ps. liii. 1' (STU-011), attached to a quotation the companion does not print. The six advisories the iteration-2 cold review left standing were not forwarded and are owed no disposition; all six are cleared. SYN-009: the scope note's text-control sentence now carries the study's bound (every Latin form of the ten proper elements), the reception paragraph discloses the tracked eCatholic2000 transcription behind Bellarmine and the web deliveries and optical text layers behind some Latin, and the References divide Augustine's Migne text from the two loci read at augustinus.it and name Bellarmine's transcription. SYN-010: the Offertory row attributes the place and hearers to the article's grounds for the traditional position instead of to 'Its grounds'. SYN-011: the Gospel row gives Jerome only what the article gives him and assigns the departure from Jerusalem to the article. SYN-012: the themes section names the change Gueranger's report depends on. SYN-013: Jerome's reason for the lawyer's question stands beside Chrysostom's, so the study's sixth narrow disagreement survives compression. SYN-014: the Alleluia row of the page-one map carries its incipit Domine, exaudi. No new evidence-dependent claim was added and no upstream defect was found, so none is reported. No research record, no study component, format.tex, proper-components.toml and web-edition.toml were touched. The additions were paid for inside the same components: the iteration-2 document held 12 pages with almost no slack and the additions first carried it to 14, so the derived prose was tightened by about the same amount in places where compression costs no attribution, locus, disagreement or qualification -- Augustine's threefold 'whole' named rather than quoted twice, and Jerome on the Abraham reading of Ps 109, the footstool clause, Chrysostom's fire and wet timber, Bellarmine's second sentence on the Gradual versicle, Hilary's rule for affliction, Durandus's promise of paradise, and the closing echo of Aquinas's beatitude (already stated with its locus in the Gradual subsection) removed, with Theodoret on lowliness, Augustine on Daniel's own sins, the Trent antidotum clause and the scope note's relation paragraph shortened. Every witness the iteration-2 document named is still named at the same loci and all six of the study's narrow disagreements are still here. Substantive word count 4,585 (4,218 with the content of the \latin{} quotations removed) over the themes and commentary components, counted through Pandoc's LaTeX AST with comments, headings and page markers removed and the \latin and \work arguments unwrapped; the same script gives the study's six argumentative components 14,024 (13,187), so the companion is a little under a third of the study's argument. summary: Re-derived the concise study of the Seventeenth Sunday after Pentecost against the expansive study as its iterations 3-7 and their cold review left it, carrying the four study changes that reach the derived argument (Chrysostom's reciprocity between the two commandments in both directions; the second reading's Postcommunion, which now gives that reading nothing of its own instead of being its third confession; Augustine's unus/unum distinction at the Alleluia; and Ps 109 given its Hebrew number at first use) and clearing all six advisories standing against the derived prose. The settled PDF is 12 physical pages with an auxiliary file byte-identical to iterations 1 and 2, so every interpretive-pagination-v1 marker stands where it stood.
